There's  this  thing  called  the  Solomon 
 Paradox,  which  is  there's  a  human 
 tendency  to  be  better  at  offering  wise 
 advice  to  others  than  it  is  to  apply 
 that  same  wisdom  to  our  own  situation  or 
 own  lives.  They  call  it  the  Solomon 
 Paradox  because  Solomon  was  this  big 
 wise  guy,  but  he  actually  his  life  was  a 
 bit  of  a  mess.  The  way  that  I  use  this 
 is  I  think  I  want  to  imagine  talking  to 
 my  85-year-old  incredibly  wise  self  or 
 at  least  wiser  than  I  am  now.  I  ask  him 
 what  he  thinks  I  should  do. 
 And  what's  weird  is  it  takes  you  out  of 
 your  current  frame  and  puts  you  in  this 
 other  frame  and  you  become  more 
 objective  about  your  current  situation.
